form.label: Rule Reference
form.description: What a rule looks for, how it runs here, and why it is trusted as much as it is. Pick a rule to read it.

search.query: | inputlookup sigma_rules.csv | eval label = sigma_platform." — ".sigma_rule." (".sigma_level.")" | sort label | table label, sigma_rule_id

| inputlookup sigma_rules.csv where sigma_rule_id="$rule_id|s$" | lookup sigma_rule_logic sigma_rule_id OUTPUT sigma_description, sigma_detection_yaml, sigma_condition, sigma_spl, sigma_scope, sigma_confidence_why, sigma_tags | lookup mitre_techniques technique_id as sigma_technique OUTPUT display_name as tech_name, url as tech_url, description as tech_desc, detection as tech_detect, data_sources as tech_sources, tactic_names as tech_tactic | eval tech_name = coalesce(tech_name, "No ATT&CK technique mapped"), tech_url = coalesce(tech_url, "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/enterprise/"), tech_desc = coalesce(tech_desc, "This rule carries no ATT&CK mapping, so there is no technique page to read."), tech_detect = coalesce(tech_detect, ""), tech_sources = coalesce(tech_sources, "not stated"), sigma_falsepositives = if(sigma_falsepositives="", "The author declared none. That is not the same as there being none.", sigma_falsepositives), sigma_references = if(sigma_references="", "", sigma_references), sigma_author = if(sigma_author="", "not stated", sigma_author), handling_note = if(sigma_disposition="immediate", "Alerts on a single match. Reserved for rules that are both severe and specific.", "Recorded and baselined rather than alerted. Its value is in the pattern, not in one occurrence."), sigma_rule_url = "https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/search?q=".sigma_rule_id

div.p: This is the author's own detection block, unchanged. Each named selection is a set of conditions; the condition line at the end states how they combine. A not in that line is an exclusion the author added after seeing a false positive.

The rule is converted to SPL and evaluated inside a batched search rather than as a search of its own. The scope ahead of it is what the log source maps to in this installation, and is what keeps the engine affordable: without it every rule would read the whole index.

p.a: Read the full technique page at attack.mitre.org →

div.h3: Why it is trusted this much
div.p: Confidence is scored from what the rule says about itself, not from how often it fires. A severe rule whose author has written down that it matches legitimate work should not wake anyone on one event; a specific rule for a named tool should.
